title: Washington, DC Trivia Night

questions.q: What do the letters in "Washington, DC" stand for?
Which river separates Washington from Arlington, Virginia?
Which French-born engineer drew up the original 1791 plan for the capital's streets and avenues?
Which country gave Washington its famous cherry trees in 1912?
Which Smithsonian museum on the National Mall displays the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer?
questions.a: The National Air and Space Museum

questions.q: Which famous blue diamond is on display at the National Museum of Natural History?
Which Washington team won its first Stanley Cup in 2018?
Which jazz composer and bandleader, born in Washington in 1899, made his name at Harlem's Cotton Club?
Chuck Brown is called the "Godfather" of which percussion-driven funk style born in Washington?
What is the name of the smoky, spicy sausage, usually served with chili and onions, that is Washington's signature local dish?

notes: District of Columbia, established by the Residence Act of 1790; see Washington, D.C. (Wikipedia) or dc.gov.
The Potomac River forms the District's southwest boundary with Virginia; Arlington lies directly across it. See Potomac River (Wikipedia) or any map.
Pierre Charles L'Enfant, born in Paris, prepared the plan in 1791 at George Washington's request; see the National Park Service 'L'Enfant Plan' page.
Gift of about 3,000 trees from the city of Tokyo, planted 27 March 1912; see the National Park Service 'History of the Cherry Trees' page.
Replaced the Smithson nationality question (born in Paris, British; arguable either way).
Hope Diamond, donated by Harry Winston in 1958, displayed at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History; see naturalhistory.si.edu.
Capitals beat the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2018 Stanley Cup Final, the franchise's first title; see NHL.com Stanley Cup history.
Edward Kennedy 'Duke' Ellington, born 29 April 1899 in Washington, led the Cotton Club orchestra from 1927; see Duke Ellington (Wikipedia) or dukeellington.com.
Chuck Brown (1936-2012), 'Godfather of Go-Go'; go-go was made DC's official music in 2020. See Go-go (Wikipedia) or Library of Congress coverage.
The half-smoke, a coarse smoked sausage, typically pork and beef, often served with chili, mustard and onions; see Half-smoke (Wikipedia).
